panels.title: Jajmani anatomy
ascii_lines: JAJMAN -> patron household, usually landholding
KAMIN -> designated hereditary service group
SERVICE -> barbering, laundry, priestly, carpentry, smithing
PAYMENT -> customary, often grain or kind, sometimes cash
MUST REMEMBER: Rural society combines caste, class, land, labour, credit, kinship, panchayat,
market and state relations; agrarian change follows tenure reform, Green Revolution,
mechanisation, commercialisation, feminisation, migration, non-farm diversification and
ecological stress.

panels.title: What actually defined jajmani
ascii_lines: NOT -> the absence of cash in the transaction
YES -> hereditary allocation of the service role
YES -> personalised patron-client obligation
YES -> caste occupation embedded in the village economy

panels.title: Decline mechanism
ascii_lines: COMMERCIALISATION -> patrons buy services in a market
NON-FARM WORK -> service castes migrate to towns for wages
DECOUPLING -> hereditary occupation-caste link breaks
RESIDUAL -> ritual and personalised ties survive in places

panels.title: Agrarian class ladder
ascii_lines: LANDOWNING CULTIVATOR -> controls land and surplus
TENANT OR SHARECROPPER -> cultivates with insecure claim
LANDLESS LABOURER -> depends on wage work
OVERLAP -> class often but not always tracks caste rank
source_references: Caste and class in the village

panels.title: Dominant caste test
ascii_lines: NUMBERS -> locally numerous population
LAND -> significant share of village land
OFFICE -> control of Panchayat and political networks
RESULT -> local power can sit below the ritual top

panels.title: Two categories kept apart
ascii_lines: DOMINANT CASTE -> caste-level, numbers plus land plus office
LANDOWNING CLASS -> economic category cutting across castes
USUAL CASE -> the two largely coincide in a village
ERROR PREVENTED -> treating them as the same unit

panels.title: Green Revolution differentiation
ascii_lines: INPUT PACKAGE -> high-yielding seed, irrigation, fertiliser
REQUIREMENT -> upfront capital, credit and market access
EFFECT -> earlier adopters capture a larger share of gains
LIMIT -> outcome varies by crop, tenancy and region

panels.title: Panchayat power test
ascii_lines: RESERVED SEAT -> Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and women
QUESTION -> who sets the agenda in practice
PROXY RISK -> informal dominant-caste network controls decisions
EVIDENCE NEEDED -> village-level, not a national statistic

panels.title: Continuum against dichotomy
ascii_lines: DICHOTOMY -> village traditional, town modern, sealed apart
CONTINUUM -> one spectrum linked by flows
FLOWS -> migration, remittance, trade, media, road and market
CAUTION -> linkage does not abolish remoteness or land relations

panels.title: Scope discipline
ascii_lines: SOCIETY OWNS -> jajmani, dominance, stratification, continuum
ECONOMY OWNS -> land ceiling, tenancy law, poverty aggregates
GOVERNANCE OWNS -> Panchayati Raj institutional design
RULE -> cross-refer the borrowing and label it
CLOSE DISTINCTION: Rural is not agricultural, landowner is not cultivator, farmer is not only
title-holder, productivity is not income, agricultural labour is not bonded labour, and
Panchayati Raj representation is not the same as effective decision-making power.
source_references: Scope discipline in a rural answer

panels.title: Measurement boundary
ascii_lines: PLFS 2023-24 -> dated rural workforce comparator
PLFS ANNUAL REPORT 2025 -> released March 2026, latest round
PERIOD -> January to December, not the older July to June cycle
LIMIT -> cannot prove jajmani decline or caste dominance
EVIDENCE LIMIT: Contrast Punjab-Haryana, eastern India, dryland Deccan, plantation, tribal and
peri-urban regions; use Agriculture Census, Situation Assessment and labour data with
period/coverage labels, and treat technology-policy correlations as mechanisms requiring
land, water, market and power analysis.

panels.title: Rural answer spine
ascii_lines: OPEN -> name the changing power relation, not a village portrait
BODY -> jajmani change, class structure, dominance, Panchayat
FRAME -> which resource now carries power in this village
CLOSE -> continuum verdict with the data and scope caveats
source_references: Answer spine and honest question status
